summary: A laid-off person who asks a close friend or relative for a lead usually gets some help, because that is where most job seekers turn first.
realLife: A Pew survey found two-thirds of recent job seekers turned to close friends or family, and one in five named them as their single most important resource.
sources: Pew Research Center, The Internet and Job Seeking: https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2015/11/19/1-the-internet-and-job-seeking/
inGame: a job-lost call from a friend or relative is already in the game; the helper's reply is a lead the receiving person's job record can use.

turns.summary: The friend calls a hiring manager and sets up an interview.
turns.writesBack: interview lead; tie closer; a promise to return the favor

turns.summary: The friend is sorry but knows of nothing.
The friend never calls back and the asker notices.
